samples.question: The picture shows a row of coloured discs standing side by side, all of them a different colour; count them, because how many discs are drawn is part of what decides the answer. The row is counted as a closed ring: counting always moves towards the right, as the grey arrow under the row shows, and after the rightmost disc still standing the count continues at the leftmost disc still standing. A single black triangle is drawn above the row: the marked disc is the disc whose centre is nearest to that triangle. The cream card at the bottom of the picture carries a number of black pips; call that number k, so k is how many pips are drawn on the card. Discs are taken away one at a time by this rule. For the first count, the marked disc is counted as one, the disc to its right is counted as two, and so on, counting k discs in all; the k-th disc counted is taken away. Every later count starts at the disc still standing that comes next to the right of the disc just taken away, counting that disc as one, and again counts k discs and takes the k-th away. Only discs still standing are ever counted: a disc that has been taken away is skipped over and is never counted again, and counting wraps from the right end of the row round to the left end as often as needed. Discs never move sideways and a disc that has been taken away never comes back. This is repeated until only one disc is left standing. The picture shows only the starting row: no disc is drawn as taken away, and neither the later rows nor the last disc is drawn anywhere in the picture. What colour is the one disc still standing at the end? Answer with one word: red, orange, yellow, green, teal, blue or purple.
